messages.subject: funny scantwo p-values
parts:
Hi all,

I have a question about the scantwo summary output:
does anyone have an explanation why R reports me p-values of 1 and 0 for the lod.int and lod.add output? This looks rather strange to me...



scan2_hk_summary <- summary(result_scan2_hk, perms = perm_scan2_hk, alpha = 0.2, pvalues=T)

pos1f pos2f lod.full pval lod.fv1 pval lod.int pval
cs12916:cs13340 92.16 74.1 10.1 0.03 4.86 0.99 1.63 1


pos1a pos2a lod.add pval lod.av1 pval
92.16 80.1 8.5 0 3.23 0.19



Thank you very much in advance for your comments!

Cheers,

Anna

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] funny scantwo p-values
parts:
The p-values are the proportion of permutation replicates with LOD scores >= the observed.
So if no permutations gave that big of a LOD score, the p-value will be 0.
If all permutations gave that big of a LOD score, the p-value will be 1.

karl
